Quezon City http: ltv.w,v. dilg.gov.ph 08 OPINION No. 1M HON. MICHAEL L. TAGAL Acting City Vice-Mayor Ozamiz City Misamis Occidental Dear Hon. Tagal: s. 2012 This has reference to your letter dated 22 March 2018 requesting this Department's opinion on whether or not you can exercise the powers and functions inherent in the Office of the (Vice-Mayor) VM pursuant to a Memorandum issued by the Office of the Regional Director, DILG-region X, dated August 4, 2017. As stated in your letter, Hon. Luansing took her oath as VM of Ozamiz City on 24 October 2017 and proclaimed herself as the VM and at the same time, the Acting City Mayor. On II March 2018, Hon. Luansing issued a Public Statement stressing that having took her oath as V M, she assumed as permanent VM and at the same time, as the Acting City Mayor, thus, disregarding the Memorandum dated 4 August 2017 issued by the DILG- Region X recognizing you as the Acting VM of Ozamiz City. Let it be noted that there was a permanent vacancy in the Office of the Mayor because former Mayor Reynaldo O. Parojinog, Sr. died. Since the successor, VM Nova Parojinog was arrested and detained for possession of illegal drugs, there arises a temporary vacancy in the Office of the Mayor. May we emphasize also that the first ranking Sangguniang Panlungsod (SP) Member Ricardo O. Parojinog has resigned. Hence, by virtue of automatic succession, this Department agrees with the Memorandum issued by DILG- Region X, recognizing the assumption of office of the second ranking, (SP) Member Luansing as Acting City Mayor (current Vice-Mayor), and you, the third ranking SP Member as Acting V M, both of Ozamiz City, Misamis Occidental. Foremost, based on the facts you presented in your letter, it appeared that there is a temporary vacancy in the Office of the Mayor because the VM who succeed to the Office of the Mayor was issued a Warrant of Arrest coupled with absence and non-performance of duties and functions. The said acts are considered "physical or legal reason" under Section

46(a) of the LGC which temporarily incapacitates the incumbent from performing his/her dutiesl. Relative to your query, may we inform you that this Department has already answered a similar query in its Legal Opinion No. 22, S.20122. We believe that the said opinion will help you solve your predicaments as stated in your letter. DILG Legal Opinion No. 22, S.2012 provides the exercise of the powers and performance Of the duties and functions of the Mayor by the VM during the time when the former is temporarily incapacitated to do the same creates a corresponding temporary vacancy in the latter's office during such contingency which may be paralleled to the case of Gamboa vs. Aguirre3, which discusses the effects of vacancy in the Office Of the Governor, viz: "A Vice-Governor who is concurrently an Acting Governor is actually a quasi-Governor. This means, that for purposes Of exercising his legislative prerogatives and powers, he is deemed as a non-member of the SP for the time being. By tradition, the offices of the provincial Governor and Vice-Governor are essentially executive in nature, whereas plain members of the provincial board perform functions partaking ofa legislative character. This is because the authority vested by law in the provincial boards involves primarily a delegation ofsome legislativepowers of Congress. Unlike under the old Code, where the Governor is not only the provincial Chief Executive, but also the presiding officer of the local legislative body, the new Code delineated the union ofthe executive-legislative powers in the provincial, city and municipal levels except in the Barangay. Under R.A. 7160, the Governor was deprived ofthepower to preside over the SP and is no longer considered a member thereof. This is clear from the law, when it provides that local legislative power shall be vested in the SP, which is the legislative body of the province, and enumerates therein its membership consisting of the: I.) Vice-Governor, as presiding officer, 2.) regular elective SP members, 3.) three elective sectoral representatives, and 4.) those ex-ofiicio members, namely: I DILG Legal Opinion No. 20, s.2013 dated 24 May 2013 2 7 March 2012 G.R. No. 134213, 20Ju1y 1999

a.) president oftheprovincial chaptei of the liga ng mga barangay, b.) president of the panlalawigang pederasyon ng Inga sangguniang kabataan, c.) president of the provincial federation of sanggunian members of municipalities and component cities. Not being included in the enumeration, the Governor is deemed excluded applying the rule in legal hermeneutics that when the la w enumerates, the law necessarily excludes. On the contrary, local executive power in the province is vested alone in the Governor. Consequently, the union of legislative-executive powers in the office of the local chief executive under the former Code has been disbanded, so that either department now comprises different and non-intermingling official personalities with the end in Vléw of ensuring a better delivery of public service and provide a system of check and balance between the two. It has been held that if a Mayor who is out of the country is considered "effectively absent", the VIZe-Mayor should discharge the duties of the mayor during the latter's absence. This doctrine should equally apply to the Vice-Governor since he is similarly situated as the VIZe-Mayor. Although it is difficult to lay down a definite rule as to what constitutes absence, yet this term should be reasonably construed to mean "effective" absence, that is, one that renders the officer concerned powerless, for the time being, to discharge the powers and prerogatives of his office. There is no vacancy whenever the office is occupied by a legally qualified incumbent. A sensu, contrario, there is vacancy when there is no person lawfully authorized to assume and exercise at present the duties of the office. (Underscoring supplied) Clearly, VIM Luansing cannot simultaneously perform the functions and duties in both the offices of the Mayor and Vice-Mayor because it would intermingle two (2) separate powers, i.e., executive and legislative, which has been delineated and vested by law to two (2) separate offices, to provide a system of checks and balances thereby ensuring a better delivery of public service. On a note, while being an Acting Mayor, the VM is legally deprive to exercise the functions appurtenant to the office of the VM by reason of the principle of separation of powers. Under 46(a) of the LGC, the VM as Acting Mayor can perform all the duties and powers pertaining to the Office Of the Mayor, except the power to appoint, suspend or dismiss employees which can only be exercised if the period of temporary incapacity exceeds thirty (30) working days. Thus, if the period of temporary incapacity exceeds thirty (30) working days, the Acting Mayor may already proceed to exercise such functions so as not to impair the delivery of vital public services. On the other hand, the highest ranking SP member, as Acting V M, can perform all the duties and powers pertaining to the Office of the VM because a designation in an acting capacity entails the exercise of the ministerial functions attached to the position, as well as, the exercise of discretion4. However, the Presiding Officership function is not automatically given to him in view of the ruling of the Supreme Court in the case Of Gamboa vs. Aguirre stating that the issue of Presiding Officership in this kind of situation Civil Service Commission Resolution No. 0007778 dated 24 March 2000, re: "Distinction between Acting and OIC"

shall be resolved by applying Section 49(b) of the LGC, in which case, the majority of those present members there being a quorum shall elect from among themselves the temporary Presiding Officer for that session. We hope to have enlightened you on the matter. Very truly yours, By Aut ri Of the Secretary: o CC: ISA) V Undersecretary RD Arnel M. Agabe Regional Director DILG-Region X (Northern Mindanao) Hon.
